id: wiki:decisions:zero-comments-extract-over-document

## Context

The project's no-comments rule originally prohibited inline comments explaining *what* code does (`// increment counter`) but carved out exceptions: doc comments (`///`, `/** */`), module docs (`//!`), section markers (`// ───`), and TODO/FIXME/HACK markers. A scan found ~1,000 comment lines across 90+ files — every category represented. The exceptions had eroded the rule.

## Decision

Zero comments. No exceptions. Every `//`, `///`, `//!`, `/** */`, `/* */`, `<!-- -->` line is a violation. TODO/FIXME/HACK markers are not exempt — file as WM tasks instead.

If a function, module, field, or block needs a comment to be understood, it should be split, extracted, or composed instead. Self-documenting names replace doc comments:

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `/// Returns true if the terminal supports Unicode` | `fn terminal_supports_unicode() -> bool` |
| `/** Cache for parsed oklch [l, c, h] components */` | `oklchCache` (field name) |
| `// ─── Input types ───` (section marker) | Split into `input_types.rs` module |
| `// Skill system` (field label) | `skill_engine: SkillEngine` (the type already says it) |
| `// TODO: implement doc history compaction` | Filed as `.wm/wiki/tasks/implement-doc-history-compaction.md` |

## Rationale

- Comments rot, drift from code, and create false confidence — doc comments are not immune
- Zero-tolerance enforcement is simpler to check (grep for `//`) than a nuanced policy
- Named functions and compositional patterns are refactor-safe and always up to date
- TODOs in code are invisible to task tracking — WM tasks are discoverable via search and graph

## Consequences

- Code becomes self-documenting by necessity — better naming and composition
- ~1,000 comment lines removed from ~90 files in one pass
- API docs must move to wiki pages (pattern/decision/concept pages) — not `///` on functions
- Generated files (e.g., wasm-pack `.d.ts`) need explicit exclusion
- `// @ts-ignore` directives are kept as compiler directives (not code comments)

## Related
- @wiki/rules/no-comments-in-code (updated to reflect this decision)
- @wiki/tasks/c19d50

## Context

The project's no-comments rule originally prohibited inline comments explaining *what* code does (`// increment counter`) but carved out exceptions: doc comments (`///`, `/** */`), module docs (`//!`), section markers (`// ───`), and TODO/FIXME/HACK markers. A scan found ~1,000 comment lines across 90+ files — every category represented. The exceptions had eroded the rule.

## Decision

Zero inline comments. Every `//` line in source code is a violation. TODO/FIXME/HACK markers are not exempt — file as WM tasks instead.

Doc comments (`///`, `//!`) are **permitted but governed** by the doc-comment-convention rule:
- Required on all `pub` items (API contracts for `cargo doc` and IDE hover)
- Forbidden on test functions, private helpers, and as disguised inline comments
- Must follow RFC 505/1574 format (third-person singular, standard sections)
- Must NOT contain spec references, implementation notes, or restatements of the signature

If a function, module, field, or block needs an inline comment to be understood, it should be split, extracted, or composed instead.

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `// increment counter` | Delete — obvious from code |
| `// ─── Input types ───` (section marker) | Extract into named function or module |
| `// TODO: implement X` | Filed as `.wm/wiki/tasks/X.md` |
| `/// Returns true if the terminal supports Unicode` | Keep — doc comment on pub fn (API contract) |
| `/// FR-2.5: resolves aliases` | Remove spec ref → `/// Resolves TypeScript path aliases.` |
| `/// #[test] fn test_foo` doc comment | Remove — test names must be self-documenting |

## Amendment (2026-08-17)

The original decision prohibited ALL doc comments (`///` is a violation). After implementing this and researching Rust ecosystem conventions (RFC 505, RFC 1574, Rust API Guidelines), doc comments were reinstated for public API items only. The doc-comment-convention rule now governs when and how to write them. The original "zero comments" remains in effect for inline `//` comments.

## Rationale

- Inline comments rot, drift from code, and create false confidence
- Zero-tolerance on inline comments is simpler to check than a nuanced policy
- Named functions and compositional patterns are refactor-safe and always up to date
- TODOs in code are invisible to task tracking — WM tasks are discoverable via search and graph
- Doc comments on pub items serve a different purpose: API contracts visible in `cargo doc` and IDE hover

## Consequences

- Code is self-documenting by necessity — better naming and composition
- API documentation lives in doc comments on pub items (governed by doc-comment-convention)
- Internal implementation details are NOT documented in code — they go in wiki pages
- Generated files (e.g., wasm-pack `.d.ts`) need explicit exclusion
- `// @ts-ignore` directives are kept as compiler directives (not code comments)
- No `#[allow(...)]` attributes anywhere (see no-allow-attributes rule)

- @wiki/rules/doc-comment-convention
- @wiki/rules/no-allow-attributes
